title: Windows PC Not Booting
description: A workstation fails to start or cannot reach the Windows sign-in screen.
problem: The Windows workstation does not complete startup and the user cannot access their desktop.
symptoms: No power, no display, or a manufacturer logo with no progress
Windows reports a boot-device error or repeatedly restarts
Startup Repair appears or the device remains on a blank screen
causes: Power, battery, dock, or peripheral fault
Incorrect boot order or an undetected storage device
Corrupted boot files or a failed recent update
Storage or other hardware failure
steps: Confirm power and isolate peripherals
Ask what changed, check the outlet, power adapter, indicator lights, and battery. Disconnect docks and nonessential USB devices, then try a known-good charger if available.
Observe and record the startup behavior
Note beep or LED codes, error messages, and whether the firmware logo appears. Check the manufacturer’s documented diagnostics; do not repeatedly force power-off.
Check firmware and storage detection
If authorized, enter UEFI/BIOS and confirm the internal drive is detected and the expected boot entry is selected. Do not change security or storage-mode settings without approval.
Use approved Windows recovery
If the drive is detected, try Windows Recovery Environment Startup Repair. Consider Safe Mode or a recent restore point only in line with backup, encryption, and organization policies.
Escalate suspected hardware or data risk
If diagnostics indicate a drive fault, unusual noises occur, or recovery risks data, stop and escalate to endpoint support before reinstalling or replacing parts.
root: A failed storage device or damaged boot configuration prevented Windows from loading. Confirm the actual cause from diagnostics; do not assume a software fault.
resolution: Restore the correct boot entry or use approved startup repair when hardware is healthy. Arrange authorized drive repair/replacement and data recovery if diagnostics report a hardware fault.
verification: Restart to the normal Windows sign-in screen
Sign in and check the user’s important files and required apps
Confirm the startup error does not recur
prevention: Keep endpoint backups and recovery keys current
Apply firmware and Windows updates through managed channels
Report recurring startup errors early
tree: Does the device power on?
No: verify outlet, adapter, dock, and battery; if still unpowered, escalate for hardware service. Yes: continue to startup observations.
Is the internal drive detected in firmware?
No: stop repeated boot attempts and escalate for storage diagnostics and data-safe repair. Yes: use approved Windows recovery.
Does Startup Repair restore boot?
Yes: verify normal startup and back up important data. No: preserve data and escalate before reset or reimage.

title: Blue Screen of Death (BSOD)
description: A stop error interrupts work and may restart the computer unexpectedly.
problem: Windows stops with a bug-check screen, causing a restart or preventing normal use.
symptoms: Blue stop screen with a stop code or QR code
Unexpected restart, possibly during a particular task
Repeated crashes after a driver, update, or hardware change
causes: Incompatible or faulty device driver
Corrupted system files or problematic update
Unstable memory, storage, overheating, or other hardware
Low disk space or third-party software conflict
steps: Capture the stop code and context
Photograph or record the stop code, time, recent changes, attached hardware, and what the user was doing. Check whether the crash repeats.
Check managed health and crash history
Review Reliability Monitor, Windows Update history, and approved endpoint-management alerts. Inspect minidumps only if authorized.
Test a recent change
If a specific driver, peripheral, or update immediately preceded the issue, follow the approved rollback or vendor remediation process.
Run supported system checks
Use organization-approved diagnostics and Windows system-file or memory checks. Check temperatures and disk health with OEM tools; avoid unapproved registry cleaners.
Escalate recurring or hardware-related crashes
Preserve diagnostic evidence and send repeated bug checks, suspected memory/storage faults, or encrypted-device issues to endpoint engineering.
root: A driver or hardware component triggered a Windows bug check; the stop code and crash evidence identify the specific cause.
resolution: Apply the verified driver/update fix or remove the confirmed faulty peripheral. If a hardware diagnostic fails, arrange authorized repair and restore the device from a known-good backup if required.
verification: Use the computer normally and repeat the activity that previously triggered the crash
Confirm no new stop errors or related health alerts
Check with the user after a reasonable observation period
prevention: Deploy signed, validated drivers through managed updates
Review crash trends rather than repeatedly reimaging
Keep backups current and ensure adequate cooling
tree: Does the stop code repeat?
No: document a one-time event and monitor. Yes: capture the exact code and continue.
Did a recent managed change precede the crash?
Yes: evaluate a supported rollback or update. No: run approved system and hardware diagnostics.
Do hardware diagnostics fail?
Yes: stop software remediation and escalate for repair. No: apply evidence-based driver or OS remediation and verify.

title: Laptop Running Extremely Slow
description: Slow sign-in, sluggish apps, or high resource use is affecting productivity.
problem: The laptop responds slowly enough to prevent the user from working efficiently.
symptoms: Long boot or sign-in time
Apps freeze or take a long time to open
High CPU, memory, disk, or network activity
causes: Resource-heavy process, too many startup apps, or low free storage
Pending updates, security scan, or sync operation
Aging hardware, overheating, or storage degradation
Malware or an unhealthy user profile
steps: Clarify when the slowdown happens
Ask when it began, whether it affects all apps, whether it follows the user across devices, and what changed recently.
Check resource use and device health
Use Task Manager and managed endpoint health reports to identify sustained CPU, memory, disk, or network pressure. Note the process and duration.
Check storage, updates, and temperature
Review available storage, pending managed updates, fan/ventilation, and OEM health alerts. Avoid deleting user data to free space.
Isolate the cause safely
Close an identified nonessential app with the user’s permission, test another network or known-good profile where approved, and run the managed security scan.
Apply supported remediation or escalate
Use approved app updates, startup configuration, storage cleanup, or hardware service. Escalate persistent high resource use or potential security findings.
root: A sustained resource bottleneck—often a resource-heavy process, constrained storage, or failing hardware—was slowing the laptop.
resolution: Resolve the evidenced bottleneck using approved software updates, managed storage cleanup, or hardware service; remove software only with the user and IT change process.
verification: Compare sign-in and app response with the original report
Confirm resource use has returned to expected levels
Ask the user to complete their normal workflow
prevention: Review device health and storage capacity regularly
Limit unnecessary approved startup applications
Keep endpoints updated and vents unobstructed
tree: Is the slowdown limited to one app?
Yes: inspect that app’s health, updates, and profile; involve its service owner if needed. No: review system-wide resource use.
Is one resource consistently saturated?
Yes: identify the responsible managed process and remediate safely. No: check storage, updates, and hardware health.
Do diagnostics suggest a hardware or security issue?
Yes: preserve evidence and escalate. No: make one supported change at a time and retest.

title: Outlook Not Sending or Receiving Emails
description: Messages are stuck in the Outbox or new email is not arriving.
problem: Outlook cannot send or receive messages as expected.
symptoms: Messages remain in the Outbox
Outlook shows disconnected or prompts repeatedly for credentials
New mail appears in webmail but not the desktop app
causes: Network connectivity or service incident
Incorrect offline mode, mailbox quota, or large attachment
Authentication, profile, or add-in issue
Incorrect mail configuration or a delivery restriction
steps: Scope the impact
Ask whether the issue affects one sender, recipient, device, or all users. Check Microsoft 365 service health using an authorized admin account.
Test the service and connection
Confirm the user has working network access and compare Outlook with Outlook on the web. Check for a service incident before changing the profile.
Inspect the Outbox and mailbox
Check Work Offline, message size, recipient address, mailbox quota, and any non-delivery report. Do not remove messages without the user’s consent.
Check authentication and client health
Confirm the user can authenticate through the approved sign-in flow. Restart Outlook and test with add-ins disabled or a new profile only under support policy.
Escalate delivery or tenant issues
Capture timestamps, affected addresses, NDR codes, and client version; route message-trace or policy issues to the Microsoft 365 administrator.
root: The desktop Outlook client was disconnected or held a message because of an oversized attachment or stale client state.
resolution: Restore the client connection, correct the message or attachment issue, and use the approved account sign-in flow. Escalate tenant delivery rules or service health issues to the messaging team.
verification: Send a small test message to an approved test mailbox
Confirm inbound mail arrives in both Outlook and webmail
Verify the original message status with the user
prevention: Use approved cloud links for large files
Monitor mailbox storage and service-health notices
Keep Outlook and Microsoft 365 apps updated
tree: Does Outlook on the web work?
No: check service health, network, and mailbox policies; escalate tenant issues. Yes: investigate the desktop client.
Is the message still in the Outbox?
Yes: check connection state, attachment size, and recipient details before retrying. No: check delivery report and message trace.
Does restarting or repairing the client resolve it?
Yes: send and receive a test message. No: collect client evidence and escalate profile or tenant issues.

title: Microsoft Teams Not Opening
description: Teams fails to launch, freezes on startup, or displays a sign-in error.
problem: The user cannot open Teams or reach their workspace.
symptoms: App spins, freezes, or closes during launch
Repeated sign-in prompts or an error message
Teams web app works while desktop app does not
causes: Service incident or network/proxy restriction
Stale sign-in token or client update issue
Damaged local app cache
Device resource or policy restriction
steps: Establish scope and check service health
Check whether the issue affects one user or multiple users and review Microsoft 365 service health.
Test connectivity and the web client
Confirm other Microsoft 365 services work and test Teams in the supported browser. Note any conditional-access or sign-in error.
Restart and update the client
Fully quit Teams, restart the device if practical, and install updates through the organization’s approved software channel.
Repair the app using managed guidance
Use the supported Windows app repair/reset procedure. Only clear app data or cache when authorized, explaining that a sign-in may be required again.
Escalate identity or service issues
Record the exact error, time, app version, and correlation ID where shown; route access-policy and tenant issues to the responsible administrator.
root: A stale client state or sign-in token prevented the desktop app from completing startup.
resolution: Update or repair Teams through the managed app process and complete the approved sign-in flow. Escalate service, identity, or access-policy errors with their correlation details.
verification: Launch Teams successfully and confirm the correct account
Test chat, meeting join, and audio device selection as relevant
Confirm the issue remains resolved after restarting Teams
prevention: Keep Teams updated through managed deployment
Use the supported sign-in process and approved network
Check service health before local troubleshooting
tree: Does Teams work in the browser?
No: check service health, network, and account access. Yes: focus on the desktop client.
Is an explicit sign-in or policy error shown?
Yes: capture the message and route to identity administration. No: restart and update the client.
Does managed app repair resolve startup?
Yes: sign in and verify core functions. No: capture app version and logs for escalation.

title: Wi-Fi Keeps Disconnecting
description: Wireless drops repeatedly, disrupting calls, browsing, and access to work.
problem: A device repeatedly loses its wireless connection during use.
symptoms: Wi-Fi icon disconnects or reconnects frequently
Calls or downloads pause when moving between areas
Other nearby users may or may not be affected
causes: Weak signal, interference, or access-point roaming
Wireless adapter driver or power-management issue
Access-point outage or capacity problem
Network authentication or DHCP lease issue
steps: Map the scope and location
Ask when and where drops occur, whether other users are affected, and whether wired access is stable. Record timestamps.
Check signal and access-point health
Compare signal in the affected location and check approved Wi-Fi controller or service-health information with the network team.
Compare another device or network
Use a known-good managed device or approved network to distinguish a device-specific issue from a site-wide issue.
Inspect adapter and authentication state
Review Windows WLAN events and adapter health. Check managed driver and power settings; do not disable enterprise security or join an unapproved network.
Escalate with evidence
Provide affected location, SSID, device identifier, timestamps, and comparison results to network operations.
root: Weak or unstable coverage in the user’s work area caused the device to roam or lose its access point.
resolution: Network operations adjusted coverage or access-point configuration for the affected area; the user tested from the same location.
verification: Maintain a connection at the affected location
Repeat a previously interrupted work task or call
Monitor for repeated drops during a normal work period
prevention: Report dead zones with location and time details
Keep managed wireless drivers current
Avoid unapproved personal hotspots for company work
tree: Are other users in the same location affected?
Yes: check for access-point or site coverage issues with network operations. No: inspect the individual device.
Does the device stay connected near an access point?
Yes: investigate coverage, roaming, or interference in the problem area. No: check adapter, driver, and authentication.
Does a managed driver update resolve it?
Yes: retest at the affected location. No: provide WLAN evidence and timestamps to network support.

title: No Internet Access After Connecting Wi-Fi
description: The device connects to Wi-Fi but cannot reach internet or work services.
problem: A wireless connection appears established, but the user cannot access internet resources.
symptoms: Connected status with a 'No internet' indicator
Some sites or company applications time out
Other devices may have working internet on the same network
causes: DHCP address, gateway, or DNS resolution problem
Captive portal or authentication not completed
Proxy, VPN, or firewall routing issue
ISP, access point, or upstream network outage
steps: Identify the affected network and scope
Confirm the SSID, affected apps, whether colleagues are affected, and whether a VPN is connected. Avoid sharing credentials over chat.
Check address and gateway state
Review the device’s IP configuration and confirm it has a valid address and default gateway. Do not expose network details publicly.
Separate DNS from connectivity
Test approved internal and external destinations using standard diagnostics. Note name-resolution versus general connectivity errors.
Check VPN, proxy, and portal state
Follow organization guidance for VPN and proxy state. Complete any legitimate guest portal sign-in; never bypass corporate controls.
Escalate upstream issues
If multiple users or the gateway are affected, send location, SSID, timestamps, and test results to network operations.
root: The connection had no usable DNS resolution or upstream gateway route, even though Wi-Fi association succeeded.
resolution: Restore the correct managed network configuration or have network operations resolve the DNS/gateway issue. Reconnect to the approved SSID after the change.
verification: Open an approved internal resource and external site
Confirm name resolution and connection are stable
Verify VPN and protected applications work as expected
prevention: Use only approved wireless networks
Report site-wide connectivity issues promptly
Keep VPN and proxy configuration managed
tree: Does the device have a valid address and gateway?
No: investigate DHCP or access-point assignment. Yes: test name resolution and route.
Can it reach an approved destination by address but not name?
Yes: investigate DNS configuration. No: check gateway, VPN, proxy, and upstream routing.
Are multiple users affected?
Yes: escalate as a network incident with location and time. No: continue device-specific managed diagnostics.

title: Printer Offline Issue
description: A shared or local printer appears offline and cannot accept print jobs.
problem: A printer is shown as offline even though the user expects it to be available.
symptoms: Printer queue reports Offline
Print jobs pause or show unavailable status
Colleagues may still be able to print
causes: Printer is powered off, asleep, or disconnected
Network address changed or printer is unreachable
Stale queue status or incorrect default printer
Print server or driver issue
steps: Confirm the printer and impact
Verify the printer name/location, whether other users are affected, and whether the device is shared or locally connected.
Check physical and panel status
Confirm power, paper, display warnings, and network cable/Wi-Fi indicators. Ask the user to check the printer without opening panels.
Check approved network reachability
Use the managed printer portal or print-server status to determine whether the device is reachable. Do not change printer network settings.
Refresh the user’s queue safely
Confirm the correct queue and default printer; clear only the affected user’s stuck jobs with their permission and refresh the queue.
Route shared-device faults to print support
Capture printer asset/name, location, panel error, and affected users for the print or network team.
root: The shared printer had lost network connectivity, causing the print queue to report it as offline.
resolution: Print support restored the printer’s managed network connection and refreshed the shared queue.
verification: Confirm the printer reports ready/online
Print a small approved test page
Check that the user’s normal queue remains available
prevention: Report printer panel or connectivity warnings promptly
Use the correct shared print queue
Keep printer network reservations and firmware managed
tree: Do other users see the printer offline?
Yes: check printer panel, network, and shared print service. No: inspect the user’s queue and workstation.
Is the printer reachable in the managed print portal?
No: escalate printer/network connectivity. Yes: refresh the affected queue and verify the driver.
Does a test page print?
Yes: have the user retry their job. No: capture queue and panel errors for print support.

title: Printer Not Printing Despite Queue
description: Print jobs appear in the queue but pages never come out of the printer.
problem: The user submits jobs to a printer queue, but output is not produced.
symptoms: Jobs remain pending, disappear without printing, or show an error
Printer is online but does not produce pages
A test page may behave differently from the user’s document
causes: Paused queue or stuck print spooler
Paper, toner, jam, or finishing warning
Incorrect driver, port, or queue selection
Print server or application-specific job issue
steps: Determine whether one user or many are affected
Check whether a test page and another user’s job print. Confirm the selected printer and whether the document is specific.
Check printer status and supplies
Review the printer panel for paper, toner, jam, or tray warnings. Ask the user not to reach into moving parts or open service panels.
Inspect the queue
Check for paused status, error details, and stuck jobs. With user approval, cancel only the affected jobs and resubmit a small test.
Check driver and server health
Use the managed queue and driver; check print-server status with print support. Avoid restarting shared services without authorization.
Escalate persistent job failures
Capture job time, application, queue name, error, and test results for print support.
root: A stuck job or printer-side supply/paper alert was holding the queue before it could process new output.
resolution: Print support cleared the confirmed blockage and restored the printer’s ready state; the user resubmitted the document after a successful test page.
verification: Print a small test page from Windows
Print a brief test from the original application
Confirm no old jobs remain stuck
prevention: Check printer readiness before resubmitting large jobs
Choose the correct tray and shared queue
Report repeating spooler or server errors
tree: Does a Windows test page print?
Yes: investigate the original application or document. No: continue queue and printer checks.
Is there a panel warning or supply issue?
Yes: follow approved consumable guidance or route for service. No: inspect the managed queue and server.
Does clearing the affected job resolve printing?
Yes: verify a fresh test. No: record error details and escalate to print support.

title: User Cannot Login to Windows
description: A user is unable to authenticate to their Windows device or account.
problem: The user cannot sign in to Windows using their assigned work account.
symptoms: Incorrect password or credentials message
Sign-in loop, temporary profile, or account restriction notice
Device is offline or not reaching the organization sign-in service
causes: Incorrect username, keyboard layout, or stale credential
Expired password, locked account, or disabled account
Network, domain-controller, or device trust issue
Conditional-access or device-compliance restriction
steps: Verify the user and exact error
Confirm identity using the organization’s approved verification process before discussing account details. Record the full error and sign-in context.
Check simple sign-in conditions
Verify username format, keyboard layout, Caps Lock, network connection, and whether the issue is at the Windows device or another service.
Check account and service status
Using authorized tools, verify account enabled/locked/expired status and identity-service health. Never ask the user to disclose their password.
Follow approved recovery
Use the organization’s verified self-service or admin reset/unlock workflow. For domain/device trust errors, follow endpoint escalation procedures.
Escalate access-policy failures
Capture correlation or sign-in log details and route device-compliance, conditional-access, or directory issues to identity administration.
root: The account was locked after repeated failed sign-ins; the lockout status was confirmed in the authorized directory console.
resolution: After verifying the user’s identity, support unlocked the account using the approved process and helped the user sign in with their own credentials.
verification: User signs in successfully on the affected device
Confirm no lockout or policy error returns
Check with the user that required work resources are accessible
prevention: Use approved password-manager and self-service tools
Report repeated or unexpected sign-in prompts
Never share passwords or verification codes with support
tree: Has the user’s identity been verified through approved channels?
No: stop and complete verification before account action. Yes: continue with the exact sign-in error.
Is the account locked, disabled, or expired?
Yes: follow the documented authorized workflow. No: investigate connectivity, device trust, and sign-in policy.
Does the issue persist after approved recovery?
Yes: collect sign-in error/correlation details and escalate. No: verify device and app access.

title: Password Reset Request
description: A user needs a secure password reset or help using self-service recovery.
problem: The user cannot authenticate and requests assistance resetting their work password.
symptoms: Password rejected or expired
Self-service reset cannot verify the user
Updated password is not accepted on one or more devices
causes: Expired or mistyped password
Self-service recovery methods are outdated
Account lockout or sign-in risk restriction
Cached credentials on a managed device
steps: Verify identity before any reset
Use the organization’s documented identity-verification procedure. Do not rely on caller ID or ask for the existing password or MFA code.
Check eligibility and account status
Using authorized tools, confirm account state and whether self-service reset is available. Check for security or risk holds.
Use approved self-service first
Guide the user to the official company password-reset portal. Never send reset links to an unverified address.
Perform an authorized admin reset if needed
Follow least-privilege reset procedure, require a user-chosen secret at next sign-in where policy requires, and communicate through an approved secure channel.
Help refresh managed sign-ins
After the user changes their password, guide them through approved device and app reauthentication; do not collect or enter their password.
root: The account password had expired and the user’s registered self-service recovery method needed updating.
resolution: The user completed the organization’s verified self-service recovery and updated their recovery methods after signing in.
verification: User signs in using their new password without disclosing it
Confirm required MFA and work applications function
Check that the account is not immediately relocked
prevention: Register and maintain approved recovery methods
Use the official self-service password reset portal
Never share passwords or MFA codes, even with support
tree: Can identity be verified via the approved process?
No: do not reset; direct the requester to the documented verification channel. Yes: continue.
Can the user use official self-service recovery?
Yes: guide them to the company portal. No: check account status and follow authorized admin reset procedure.
Does sign-in still fail after recovery?
Yes: investigate lockout, MFA, cached credentials, and risk policy without collecting secrets. No: confirm recovery methods.

title: Active Directory Account Locked
description: A repeatedly locked directory account prevents access to workplace resources.
problem: An Active Directory account is repeatedly locked, interrupting user access.
symptoms: User receives account-locked messages across services
Unlocking temporarily restores access, then lockout returns
Authentication failures may occur while user is away
causes: Stale credentials saved on a device or service
Mapped drive, scheduled task, or mobile app retrying an old password
Repeated incorrect sign-in attempts
Potential suspicious sign-in activity
steps: Verify the user and confirm lockout scope
Complete approved identity verification and determine which services/devices are affected. Do not repeatedly unlock without investigating.
Check lockout events using authorized tools
Review domain-controller lockout logs and approved account lockout tools for timestamps and source workstation.
Identify stale credentials safely
Check the identified device’s Credential Manager and approved services, scheduled tasks, mapped drives, or mobile clients with the user/IT owner.
Assess security indicators
If source, time, or behavior is unexpected, preserve logs and follow the security incident process before clearing credentials.
Remove the confirmed cause and unlock
After addressing the source and following approval, unlock once using authorized directory tooling and monitor for recurrence.
root: A saved credential on a mapped resource repeatedly retried an outdated password and triggered the directory lockout policy.
resolution: The stale saved credential was removed from the confirmed source. Authorized support unlocked the account and monitored for repeat failures.
verification: User authenticates to required services
Check for new lockout events after the source is corrected
Confirm the user recognizes recent sign-in activity
prevention: Update saved credentials when passwords change
Review unattended devices and service accounts
Escalate unrecognized authentication activity promptly
tree: Is the lockout source familiar and expected?
No: preserve evidence and follow the security incident process. Yes: continue to isolate the source.
Do logs identify a workstation or service?
Yes: check its saved credentials, tasks, and mapped resources with the owner. No: gather additional authorized sign-in telemetry.
Does lockout stop after the credential source is corrected?
Yes: unlock once and monitor. No: do not loop unlocks; escalate to directory/security operations.

title: Mapped Drive Not Accessible
description: A mapped network drive is missing, unavailable, or showing an access error.
problem: A user cannot reach a mapped company file share from Windows.
symptoms: Mapped drive shows a red X or is absent
Access denied or network path not found
Share works for colleagues or from another network location
causes: VPN or office network not connected
File server/share unavailable
Expired credentials or changed permissions
Stale drive mapping or DNS issue
steps: Confirm share, user, and scope
Record the approved share path, exact error, affected user, network location, and whether colleagues can access it.
Check required network access
Confirm the user is on the corporate network or approved VPN and that other company resources work.
Test server and name resolution
Use approved tools to check the file service and server name. Determine whether the issue is connectivity, name resolution, or access denied.
Verify access and refresh the mapping
Ask the share owner or authorized administrator to confirm permissions. Reconnect using the documented managed mapping; do not broaden access.
Escalate server-side faults
Provide the share path, error, timestamps, and user/device details to file services or network support.
root: The user was outside the corporate network without the approved VPN connection needed to reach the file server.
resolution: The user reconnected through the approved corporate VPN and reopened the managed drive mapping.
verification: Open the intended folder and a permitted file
Confirm read/write access matches the user’s role
Ensure the mapping reconnects after sign-in if policy requires
prevention: Use the approved VPN when working remotely
Request access through the share owner, not informal workarounds
Use managed drive mappings and report outages
tree: Is the user on the approved corporate network or VPN?
No: connect using the managed VPN and retest. Yes: continue to server reachability.
Does the share path resolve and respond?
No: investigate DNS, VPN routing, or file-service availability. Yes: check user permissions.
Is access denied?
Yes: route to the share owner for least-privilege permission review. No: refresh the managed mapping and verify.

title: VPN Connection Failure
description: The managed VPN client fails to connect or disconnects shortly after connecting.
problem: The user cannot establish or maintain an approved remote-access VPN session.
symptoms: Authentication, certificate, or gateway error
Connection stalls or disconnects repeatedly
VPN connects but internal work resources remain unavailable
causes: VPN service incident or network restriction
MFA, account, certificate, or device-compliance issue
Outdated managed VPN client
Conflicting network state or home-router issue
steps: Capture error and scope
Record the exact error, time, client version, network type, and whether other approved services work. Check VPN service status.
Verify account and device posture
Confirm the user can complete approved MFA and that the managed device is compliant. Never request an MFA code.
Check client and network prerequisites
Use the managed app portal to confirm VPN client version. Test a permitted alternate network only when policy allows.
Retry using documented connection steps
Restart the client or device when appropriate and use the assigned gateway/profile. Do not disable security software or install unapproved VPN tools.
Escalate with diagnostics
Collect approved VPN logs, error codes, and device compliance details for network or identity operations.
root: The device’s VPN client was outdated and failed the organization’s managed connection requirements.
resolution: The current VPN client was installed from the company portal, then the user completed MFA and connected to the assigned gateway.
verification: VPN reports connected with the expected profile
Open an approved internal resource
Confirm the connection remains stable during the user’s workflow
prevention: Keep the managed VPN client updated
Use the assigned gateway and MFA process
Report repeated disconnects with timestamps
tree: Is the VPN service experiencing an incident?
Yes: communicate the status and follow incident guidance. No: continue.
Does the user pass approved MFA and device-compliance checks?
No: route to identity or endpoint compliance support. Yes: inspect client version and connection logs.
Does the managed client connect but internal resources fail?
Yes: escalate routing/DNS policy to network operations. No: verify a successful session and retest.

title: Laptop Camera Not Working
description: The built-in or external camera is unavailable in a meeting or camera app.
problem: The user cannot use the expected camera on their work laptop.
symptoms: Camera missing, blocked, or showing a black preview
An app reports the camera is in use or unavailable
Camera works in one app but not another
causes: Physical privacy shutter or camera key is off
App camera permission or device selection issue
Another application is using the camera
Driver, firmware, or hardware failure
steps: Identify whether the camera is built-in or external
Ask which app, when the issue began, and whether a physical privacy shutter or camera indicator is present.
Check privacy and device selection
Open the physical shutter or function-key camera control; confirm the correct camera is selected in Windows and the meeting app.
Review Windows privacy permissions
Check camera permission for the intended app through Windows Settings and the organization’s privacy policy.
Test a second approved app and inspect device status
Close other meeting apps, test Windows Camera if permitted, and check Device Manager/OEM diagnostics for errors.
Update through managed support or escalate hardware
Use the approved driver/firmware update channel; route persistent missing devices or physical damage for repair.
root: The camera’s physical privacy shutter was closed, so Windows and meeting apps could not access the image.
resolution: The user opened the integrated privacy shutter and selected the built-in camera in the meeting application.
verification: Confirm a live preview in an approved camera app
Join a test meeting and verify the camera indicator
Check that the camera privacy setting remains user-controlled
prevention: Check the shutter and device selection before meetings
Keep camera drivers managed and current
Protect the lens and report hardware damage
tree: Is the physical shutter or camera key off?
Yes: re-enable it and test preview. No: continue.
Does camera work in a second approved app?
Yes: inspect permissions and selection in the original app. No: check Windows privacy settings and Device Manager.
Does the device show a hardware error?
Yes: capture the device status and arrange repair. No: use managed driver support and verify.

title: Microphone Not Detected
description: A headset or built-in microphone does not appear as an available input.
problem: The user cannot select or use the expected microphone for calls or recordings.
symptoms: Input device absent from app settings
No input level or microphone test response
App uses the wrong microphone or reports permission denied
causes: Muted headset, disconnected cable, or Bluetooth pairing issue
Incorrect input selection or app permission
Audio driver or Bluetooth service problem
Hardware fault or disabled device
steps: Clarify the microphone and app
Identify the built-in, USB, or Bluetooth microphone and whether it fails in one app or everywhere.
Check physical controls and connection
Confirm mute switch, cable/USB connection, battery, and Bluetooth pairing. Reconnect only after checking active calls.
Select the correct input and test it
In Windows sound settings and the meeting app, choose the intended input and observe the input-level meter.
Review app permissions and device status
Check Windows microphone privacy permission and Device Manager. Avoid changing enterprise audio policies.
Apply managed updates or test known-good hardware
Use approved audio/Bluetooth drivers and compare with a known-good headset; escalate persistent hardware faults.
root: The headset’s inline mute switch was enabled, leaving the selected microphone with no input.
resolution: The user released the headset mute switch and selected the headset microphone as the input device.
verification: Confirm the Windows input meter responds to speech
Make an approved test call and confirm clear two-way audio
Verify the app retains the correct input device
prevention: Check headset mute and battery before calls
Set the preferred device in meeting-app settings
Keep approved audio drivers and firmware current
tree: Does Windows list the intended microphone?
No: check cable, pairing, mute, and Device Manager. Yes: select it and test input level.
Does the Windows input meter respond?
No: inspect physical mute, permission, and driver. Yes: check the meeting app’s selected input and permission.
Does a known-good headset work?
Yes: isolate the original headset. No: investigate managed audio drivers or endpoint hardware.

title: Second Monitor Not Detected
description: An external display remains blank or does not appear in display settings.
problem: A laptop or desktop does not detect or display on a connected second monitor.
symptoms: Monitor reports no signal
Windows does not show a second display
Display flickers or works only at a lower resolution
causes: Monitor input or power setting
Loose/damaged cable, adapter, or dock
Unsupported resolution or display mode
Graphics driver, dock firmware, or hardware issue
steps: Confirm display and connection details
Identify the monitor, cable, adapter, dock, and whether the setup worked previously.
Check power, input, and cable seating
Confirm monitor power and selected input, reseat both cable ends, and test a known-good compatible cable where available.
Check Windows display mode
Use Windows display settings to detect the display and select Extend/Duplicate. Start at a supported resolution and refresh rate.
Isolate dock, port, and monitor
Test one display at a time, use a direct laptop port if supported, or compare with a known-good monitor/dock.
Update managed graphics or dock firmware
Use OEM/organization-approved updates and escalate suspected port, dock, or monitor hardware failure.
root: The dock’s display cable was connected to an incompatible adapter port, preventing Windows from detecting the monitor.
resolution: The display cable was connected to the dock’s supported video output and the correct monitor input was selected.
verification: Confirm both displays appear in Windows display settings
Check the requested layout, resolution, and orientation
Reconnect the dock once to confirm the display returns
prevention: Use approved docks, cables, and adapters
Label workstation-specific video connections
Keep dock and graphics updates managed
tree: Does the monitor show its own menu?
No: check monitor power or hardware. Yes: verify selected input and cable.
Does a direct connection work?
Yes: isolate dock, adapter, or cable. No: inspect port, graphics settings, and driver.
Does Windows detect the display after a managed update?
Yes: verify arrangement and resolution. No: document hardware tested and escalate.

title: USB Device Not Recognized
description: A USB accessory or storage device fails to appear or prompts an error.
problem: Windows does not recognize a connected USB device or cannot use its expected function.
symptoms: USB notification reports an unrecognized device
Device absent from File Explorer or Device Manager
Device connects intermittently or only on one port
causes: Cable, connector, or device power problem
USB controller or device driver fault
Device incompatibility or policy restriction
Hardware failure
steps: Identify the device and business purpose
Confirm device type, owner, whether it contains data, and whether it is approved for company use.
Check physical connection safely
Inspect for visible damage, try a known-good approved cable/port, and avoid hubs when isolating power issues.
Check Windows device status
Review Device Manager for error codes and Windows notifications. Do not format a storage device or ignore security prompts.
Compare a known-good port/device
Test with a known-good approved accessory and, if permitted, compare the original device on another managed computer.
Apply policy-approved driver support or escalate
Use managed driver updates; route unknown/unapproved storage or suspected hardware failure to security or endpoint support.
root: A damaged USB cable caused intermittent enumeration, so Windows could not maintain a stable connection to the accessory.
resolution: The damaged cable was replaced with an organization-approved cable and the device was reconnected to a direct USB port.
verification: Confirm the correct device appears without warnings
Test its expected function or read-only access as appropriate
Reconnect once and confirm stable detection
prevention: Use approved accessories and cables
Avoid damaged connectors and unsupported hubs
Never format or copy data from unknown devices without authorization
tree: Is the device approved for company use?
No or unknown: stop and check policy/security before connecting. Yes: continue.
Does a known-good cable/port detect it?
Yes: replace the faulty connection component. No: check Device Manager and device policy.
Is it a storage device with important data?
Yes: do not format; preserve data and escalate. No: use managed driver support or hardware service.

title: Windows Update Failure
description: A managed Windows update fails, rolls back, or remains pending.
problem: Windows Update cannot install an expected update on the user’s device.
symptoms: Update error code or repeated retry
Installation stuck or rolled back after restart
Device remains behind the organization’s update baseline
causes: Insufficient free space or interrupted restart
Update service or component-store issue
Network, proxy, or management-policy restriction
Driver incompatibility or pending reboot
steps: Record the error and update context
Capture the KB/update ID, exact error code, time, device build, and whether a restart is pending.
Check managed update status and service health
Review endpoint-management compliance and update-ring status; confirm whether the issue affects multiple devices.
Check prerequisites and available storage
Confirm power, network, free space, and pending restart. Do not delete system files or disable endpoint security.
Use supported Windows remediation
Run the organization-approved troubleshooter or repair workflow and retry through the managed update channel.
Escalate repeated or fleet-wide failures
Provide update IDs, error codes, device build, and management status to endpoint engineering.
root: The device lacked sufficient free disk space to stage the cumulative update successfully.
resolution: Approved temporary files were removed using Windows storage cleanup after user data was checked, and the managed update installed on retry.
verification: Confirm update history shows successful installation
Verify the device reports compliant in management
Check that normal startup and required apps still work
prevention: Maintain reasonable free storage capacity
Restart devices when prompted by managed updates
Monitor compliance deadlines and report repeat errors
tree: Is the device managed and receiving the correct update ring?
No: route policy/enrollment to endpoint administration. Yes: continue.
Is there a pending restart or low storage?
Yes: address safely and retry the managed update. No: capture error code and check update service status.
Do multiple devices show the same failure?
Yes: escalate as a deployment issue. No: collect device-specific logs for endpoint engineering.

title: Company Software Installation Failed
description: An approved company application fails to install from the managed software portal.
problem: The user cannot install or update an application provided by the organization.
symptoms: Company Portal reports a failed installation
Installer exits with an error or rolls back
App installs but will not launch
causes: Device not synced, compliant, or assigned the app
Insufficient storage or pending restart
Installer dependency, version conflict, or detection-rule issue
Network or software deployment service interruption
steps: Confirm the app and approved source
Verify the exact app/version and that it is assigned to the user/device in the company’s software catalog.
Capture the error and deployment status
Record the portal status, error code, time, device name, and whether other users report the same issue.
Check device prerequisites
Confirm management sync, compliance, available storage, network access, and pending restart without bypassing policy.
Retry using the managed deployment workflow
Sync the company portal and retry once after prerequisites are met. Avoid downloading installers from third-party sites or using admin credentials outside policy.
Escalate packaging or assignment issues
Send deployment logs and error details to endpoint/software packaging support if a managed retry fails.
root: The application was not assigned to the user’s device in endpoint management, so the portal could not install it.
resolution: The application owner approved the required assignment; endpoint management synced the device and deployed the app through Company Portal.
verification: Company Portal reports installation complete
Launch the app and sign in using the approved account
Confirm the installed version matches the approved release
prevention: Request software through the approved catalog
Keep device enrollment and sync healthy
Report repeat installation failures with app/version and error code
tree: Is the app available in the approved software catalog?
No: route a request through the app owner and approval workflow. Yes: continue.
Is the device managed, compliant, and synced?
No: resolve enrollment/compliance through endpoint support. Yes: review assignment and installer status.
Does a managed retry fail with the same error?
Yes: preserve deployment logs and escalate to packaging support. No: launch and verify the approved version.
